summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update16.json → valid=true). Read the captured design documents for statements bearing on the recorded findings, with three outcomes. (1) A source-explained negative that closes one of my own earlier suspicions: membership.md states that a new configuration is in effect as soon as it is appended (not when committed), that at most one configuration may be uncommitted at a time, and that the latest configuration is almost always the one used (membership.md:15, 21-26) — which is exactly the shape the shipped gating and commitment behaviour implement, so the 'uncommitted membership change narrows the majority needed for progress' behaviour is documented design, not a defect, and no recorded finding depends on the contrary. (2) Independent requirement anchoring for the non-voter transfer finding: the same document defines a Nonvoter as a member that 'receives log entries but is not considered for elections or commitment purposes' (membership.md:11-19), matching the API documentation's graceful-failure promise, so that finding's requirement no longer rests on a single doc comment. (3) A documented drift recorded as not-a-defect: the proposal says GetConfiguration waits for the latest configuration to commit and returns the committed one (membership.md:33), while the shipped method documents and implements returning the latest, possibly uncommitted, configuration (api.go:895-903) — the shipped documentation is the contract, and the proposal also differs from the code elsewhere (it presents AddVoter as staging-oriented and deprecates nothing), so this is proposal-versus-implementation drift; the proposal is explicitly treated as intent evidence only, not as a specification (its catch-up rule is labelled a placeholder). Recorded as two Facts, one investigation, and an 'explained' interpretation with counterevidence and limits.
